title: Scope the projection lock to the record actually written — lane mutations off the 'state' lock
action: FIX-FIRST for the red splr-1 left behind. splr-1 wrapped ALL of withMutationLock's workflow branch in withStoreLock(root,'state',...). That is over-broad: the LANE path (writeLaneRecordThroughProjection -> rebuildLaneProjection -> writeLane) writes ONLY lanePath(root, feature) (state.mjs:1704) and never .bee/state.json, so forcing it through 'state' made a correct, live invariant go red — packages/bee/tests/test_cli_state.mjs 'multisession-native-10 (invariant 1/2, C4): a lane mutation with a live workflow record never needs the shared state lock' went from near-instant to 4995ms (the lock timeout), cascading 4 more rows red in packages/bee/tests/test_msn_invariants.mjs. (1) Narrow the lock to the record actually written: default-record mutations keep 'state'; lane-routed mutations take a lane-scoped store lock instead (name it consistently, e.g. lane:<feature>), never 'state'. Decide the seam yourself — resolveMutationLockFeature already peeks at whether the target is a lane, so the lock name can be chosen at the same place the workflow lock is chosen (bee.mjs withMutationLock). (2) Apply the SAME record-scoping to the other two seams splr-1 changed: handleStateStartFeature (bee.mjs, its lane branch rebuilds a lane projection, its default branch rebuilds state.json) and handleStatePlanRevBump (lane-only by refusal, so it must take lane:<feature>, not 'state' — but KEEP its repaired workflow:<id>-before-projection-lock order, which is the whole point of the advisor's required change). handleStateRebuildProjections rebuilds state.json AND every lane, so it needs 'state' plus each lane's lock, or a documented reason it is safe with 'state' alone. (3) The global lock order must remain single and acyclic: workflow:<id> -> {state | lane:<feature>}. Never the reverse, and never lane:<feature> -> state or state -> lane:<feature> unless you take them in one fixed documented order and say so. (4) Extend scripts/tests/test_state_projection_race.mjs so it proves BOTH halves: a default-record writer still serializes on 'state', AND a lane mutation is NOT blocked by an externally-held 'state' lock (the invariant splr-1 broke) — the second assertion must fail against splr-1's code. (5) Re-vendor and regen in order: node scripts/render_plugin_skill_trees.mjs, node packages/bee/scripts/onboard_bee.mjs --repo-root . --apply, node scripts/impact_registry.mjs --write, node scripts/release_manifest.mjs --write. (6) The verify for this cell is the FULL suite, not an impacted run — splr-1 capped false-green precisely because --impacted-from-git selected 0 suites after its commit.

truths: packages/bee/tests/test_cli_state.mjs passes in full, including 'a lane mutation with a live workflow record never needs the shared state lock', with no edit to that test.
Default-record mutations still serialize on 'state' — the GH #70 proof in scripts/tests/test_state_projection_race.mjs still passes and still fails against pre-splr-1 code.
The race suite gains an assertion that a lane mutation is not blocked by an externally-held 'state' lock, and that assertion fails against splr-1's committed code (report that red output).
handleStatePlanRevBump still acquires workflow:<id> BEFORE its projection lock — the advisor-required order repair from splr-1 is preserved.
The global lock order is single and acyclic and is stated in a comment at the seam.
node scripts/run_verify.mjs (FULL, not impacted) exits 0, and its summary line is reported verbatim.
md5sum of .bee/bin/bee.mjs equals packages/bee/bee.mjs after re-vendoring.
prohibitions: Do NOT edit, weaken, skip, or delete packages/bee/tests/test_cli_state.mjs or test_msn_invariants.mjs — they encode correct behavior; the code is what was wrong.
Do NOT revert splr-1 wholesale — its state.json serialization and its plan-rev-bump order repair are both correct and must survive.
Do NOT acquire a lock inside rebuildStateProjection or rebuildLaneProjection.
Do NOT cap on an impacted run; this cell's verify is the full suite.

verify: node scripts/ledger_parity.mjs --check && node scripts/release_manifest.mjs --check && node scripts/run_verify.mjs
